bookTitle: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis

facts.statement: Richard Wyckoff began working on Wall Street as a stock runner at age 15 in 1888, opened his own brokerage at 25, launched The Ticker magazine in 1907, and published his correspondence course in the early 1930s, establishing the foundational blueprint for Volume Price Analysis.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Richard Wyckoff, who could be considered to be the founding father of volume and price analysis... started work on Wall Street as a stock runner at the age of 15 in 1888.

facts.topic: Wyckoff's Law of Supply and Demand
facts.statement: When demand exceeds supply, prices rise to meet demand; when supply exceeds demand, prices fall so oversupply is absorbed. Analogous to winter sales where falling prices attract buyers to clear inventory, price bars reflect this minute-by-minute battle.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: When demand is greater than supply, then prices will rise to meet this demand, and conversely when supply is greater then demand then prices will fall... Consider the winter sales!

facts.topic: Wyckoff's Law of Cause and Effect
facts.statement: Every market effect (price trend) requires a preceding cause, and the resulting trend is directly proportional to that cause. Extended sideways consolidation phases of accumulation or distribution generate dramatic, long-lasting trend reversals, whereas brief consolidations yield minor moves.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: In order to have an effect, you must first have a cause, and furthermore, the effect will be in direct proportion to the cause.

facts.statement: Coulling illustrates Cause and Effect through two physical analogies: a massive wave at sea rolling a vessel violently compared to a small wave, and winding a clockwork model car mechanism to maximum capacity so it travels the furthest possible distance.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The simplest analogy here is of a wave at sea. A large wave hitting a vessel will see the ship roll violently, whereas a small wave would have little or no effect.

facts.statement: Like dropping a stone in a pond where ripples expand outward, market sentiment starts on fast timeframes (5-minute) and ripples outward to slower timeframes (30-minute). VPA evaluates Micro (single candle), Macro (adjacent candles), and Global (full chart) structures.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: VPA evaluates individual candles (Micro), surrounding adjacent candles (Macro), and full chart trend history (Global) to determine the scale of the cause.

facts.topic: Wyckoff's Law of Effort vs Result
facts.statement: Mirroring Newton's third law of physics, market effort (volume) must be reflected in the consequent result (price spread). A trader acts like a forensic crime scene investigator, auditing every price bar to verify whether effort and result are in harmony.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: This is Wyckoff's third law which is similar to Newton's third law of physics. Every action must have an equal and opposite reaction. In other words, the price action on the chart must reflect the volume action below.

facts.statement: Effort and result are in harmony when a wide price spread is accompanied by high volume, confirming genuine institutional trend continuation, or when a narrow price spread is paired with low volume, confirming quiet, valid market consolidation without manipulation.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Wide price spread + high volume = Effort matched by result; confirms genuine trend continuation. Narrow price spread + low volume = Small effort matched by small result.

facts.topic: Wide Spread on Low Volume Anomaly
facts.statement: A wide price spread occurring on low volume represents a major VPA anomaly—achieving a big price result with little volume effort. This signals an artificial fake move or liquidity trap engineered by market makers rather than genuine institutional participation.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Wide price spread + low volume = Big result with little effort; indicates a fake move or trap by market makers testing liquidity.

facts.topic: Narrow Spread on High Volume Anomaly
facts.statement: A narrow price spread on high or ultra-high volume represents massive effort yielding little result, like flooring a car's gas pedal on an icy hill while the wheels spin in place. It signals heavy insider absorption presaging an imminent reversal.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Flooring the gas pedal (high effort/volume) on a steep, icy road while the car's wheels spin without moving forward (narrow price spread) signals that the vehicle has hit resistance.

facts.statement: Introduced in the mid-1860s, the telegraphic ticker tape printed real-time symbols, trade sizes, and prices. Wyckoff defined tape reading as rapid-fire horse sense—acting like a department store manager tracking inventory turnover to deduce whether insiders are accumulating or distributing.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Tape Reading is rapid-fire horse sense. Its object is to determine whether stocks are being accumulated or distributed, marked up or down, or whether they are neglected by the large interests.

facts.statement: Starting at age 15 at Paine Webber, Jesse Livermore mastered tape reading to spot institutional weakness, making over $3 million shorting the 1907 panic and approximately $100 million shorting the October 29, 1929 crash across symbols like X, GT, R, and WX.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Livermore anticipated the October 1929 collapse through tape reading, executing massive short positions that generated approximately $100 million in profits.

facts.statement: In The Wall Street Jungle (1970) and The Wall Street Gang (1974), Richard Ney exposed exchange specialists as merchants rather than impartial agents. Specialists accumulate stock inventory at wholesale prices during public panic and distribute it at retail prices during euphoria.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: As merchants, specialists will expect to sell at retail what they have bought at wholesale.

facts.topic: Ney's Laws of Capital and Media
facts.statement: Ney's first four laws state that specialists sell wholesale inventory at retail, accumulate massive capital over time requiring larger inventory cycles, leverage expanding communications media to heighten demand-supply volatility, and utilize mass media to distribute huge stock quantities to retail.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The longer the specialists remain in business, the more money they will accumulate to buy stock at wholesale, which they will then want to sell at retail.

facts.topic: Ney's Laws of Shakes and Distribution
facts.statement: Ney's laws five through eight state that deploying larger capital forces specialists to engineer deeper price declines to shake out stock, stage dramatic upside advances to attract buyers, spend longer durations distributing active stocks, and trigger broader economic breakdowns.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: In order to employ ever increasing financial resources, specialists will have to effect price declines of ever increasing dimensions in order to shake out enough stock.

facts.statement: On November 22, 1963, following President Kennedy's assassination, the AT&T specialist rapidly dropped the stock from $138 to $130 to absorb panic selling at wholesale, closed the exchange early, and reopened on November 25 at $140 for a $25,000 profit.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: The specialist in AT&T (Telephone) dropped the stock price rapidly from $138 to $130 to absorb public panic selling... and reopened on November 25 at $140, capturing a $25,000 profit.

generalAssumptions: Market price manipulation is structurally transparent on the volume tape.
Effort versus result governs institutional capital movement.
